module.description: Implement a simplified radix-2 divider on 8-bit signed or unsigned integers. and the inputs are two 8-bit operands. The module accepts a dividend and a divisor as inputs and provides a 16-bit result containing both the quotient and the remainder. The design supports both signed and unsigned division operations.

ports.input: Clock signal used for synchronous operation.
The reset signal to initialize or reset the module.
1-bit indicates if the operation is signed (1) or unsigned (0).
8-bit input signal representing the dividend for division.
8-bit input signal representing the divisor for division.
1-bit indicates that a valid operation request is present.
1-bit indicates that the 16-bit output result has already been acknowledged.
ports.output: 1-bit output signal indicating the result is valid and ready. res_valid must be constructed as combinational logic and not in any always block. So `res_valid` must not be declared as register.
16-bit the output containing the remainder in the upper 8 bits and the quotient in the lower 8 bits.

logic_description.description: Notice that below descriptions are along with tags <logic />. These tags <logic /> could be described more detail in the below description in the <implementation /> tag. With a <logic type="combinational_logic" />, must construct this logic as interal wire declaration. Or this <logic type="combinational_logic" /> can be declared as a `reg` but only be used in always(*) block. With a <logic type="sequential_logic" />, must construct this logic as `reg` declaration. Must update this logic, in an always block, based on other <logic type="sequential_logic" /> or <logic type="combinational_logic" /> states. With a <logic type="sequential_logic_operation" />, place directly this operation sequence in below mentioned description. With a <logic type="combinational_logic_operation" />, based on the keyword `assign` to construct description of this combinational logic operation.
logic_description.logic: 9-bit combinational logic. <logic refid="divisor_extend"> is set to concatenation of bit 1 and input <input refid="divisor"> if the input <input refid="sign"> and MSB of input <input refid="divisor"> is high. Otherwise, <logic refid="divisor_extend"> is set to concatenation of bit 0 and input <logic refid="divisor">.
9-bit sequencial logic. Follow the below description in the <implementation /> tag for more detail in this sequential logic.
10-bit combinational logic. This is combinational, not sequential_logic.
9-bit combinational logic. <logic refid="sub_result"> is the first 9-bit of <logic refid="all_sub_result">.
10-bit combinational <logic refid="all_sub_result"> is set to summation of <logic refid="REMAINER"> and <logic refid="NEG_DIVISOR">.
8-bit combinational logic. This is a subsection of 8-bit MSB of <logic refid="SR">.
8-bit combinational logic. This is a subsection of 8-bit LSB of <logic refid="SR">.
1-bit combinational logic. <logic refid="CO"> is set to the MSB of <logic refid="all_sub_result">.
9-bit combinational logic. If <logic refid="CO"> is high, <logic refid="mux_result"> is set to <logic refid="sub_result"> else set to <logic refid="REMAINER">.
7-bit combinational logic. <logic refid="quotient_shift"> is set to 7 bits [7:1] of <logic refid="SR">.
First, the 8-bit MSB of <logic refid="SR"> is set to 8-bit <logic refid="mux_result">. Then bit [0:0] of <logic refid="SR"> is set to <logic refid="CO">.
Concatenate <logic refid="SR"> from of first 7-bit of <logic refid="mux_result">, 7-bit <logic refid="quotient_shift">, 1-bit <logic refid="CO">, and 1-bit zero.

8-bit combinational logic. If <input refid="sign"> and the MSB of input <input refid="dividend"> is high, <logic refid="dividend_abs"> is set to two's complement of the input <input refid="dividend">. Otherwise <logic refid="dividend_abs"> is set to the original input <logic refid="dividend"> only.

8-bit combinational logic. <logic refid="final_remainer"> is set to two's complement of <logic refid="REMAINER"> if the <input refid="sign"> bit and MSB of register <input refid="dividend"> is high. Otherwise, <logic refid="final_remainer"> is set to <logic refid="REMAINER">.

8-bit combinational logic. <logic refid="final_quotient"> is set to two's complement of <logic refid="QUOTIENT"> if <logic refid="is_final_quotient_sign"> is high. Otherwise, <logic refid="final_remainer"> is set to <logic refid="QUOTIENT">.

1-bit combinational logic. <logic refid="is_final_quotient_sign"> is result of the `and` logic of <input refid="sign"> and the `xor` logic of MSB of <input refid="dividend"> register and MSB of <logic refid="divisor"> register.
1-bit sequential logic. When <input refid="rst"> is high, <input refid="start_cnt"> is reset to 0. Otherwise, follow the below description in the <implementation /> tag.

1-bit sequential logic. Must construc <logic refid="res_valid"> in a separate always block executing when positive edge of <input refid="clk"> and positive edge of <input refid="rst">. <logic refid="res_valid"> is managed based on the <input refid="rst"> signal, the cnt, and whether the result has been consumed, which is signaled by the input <input refid="res_ready">. <logic refid="res_valid"> should be update directly, without passing middle register value. <logic refid="res_valid"> is set to zero if <input refid="rst"> is high. Otherwise, if `cnt` reaches 8, <logic refid="res_valid"> is set to 1. Otherwise, if <logic refid="res_valid"> and <input refid="res_ready"> is all high, <logic refid="res_valid"> is set to 0. Otherwise, <logic refid="res_valid"> is set to <logic refid="res_valid">.

module.implementation:
Operation Start: When <input refid="opn_valid"> is high, <output refid="res_valid"> is low, and <input refid="start_cnt"> is low, the module saves the inputs dividend and divisor in to 2 8-bit corresponding regisers. Initializes the 16-bit shift register SR with the absolute value of the original input `dividend` (dividend_abs) shifted left by one bit. 9-bit NEG_DIVISOR is set to `divisor_extend`, if the sign bit and MSB of divisor is high. Otherwise, sets 9-bit NEG_DIVISOR to two's complement of the `divisor_extend`. Sets the 4-bit counter cnt to 1 and <input refid="start_cnt"> to 1 to begin the division process.
Division Process(If <input refid="start_cnt"> is high, the module performs the following steps): If most significant bit of cnt is set (the counter cnt reaches 8), the division is complete: cnt and <input refid="start_cnt"> are cleared. Then, based on SR_final_update method, Updates the shift register SR with the final remainder and quotient. Otherwise, the counter cnt is incremented, and the shift register SR is updated based on the subtraction result `mux_result`: Based on `sub_remainer_reg_divisor`, compute the summation of `NEG_DIVISOR` and `REMAINER`. Uses a multiplexer to select the appropriate result based on the carry-out. Based on `SR_shifting`, updates SR.
Result operation: The output `result` is constructed as combinational logic and is set to concatenation of `final_remainer` and `final_quotient`. Notice that, because of combinational operation, the `result` must not be calculated in any always block.
